title: Load balancer failure without health checks
question: What happens to requests when Server B crashes and the load balancer never notices?
description: Baseline for the health-check lesson. Server B crashes at 20 s and recovers at 40 s. Health checks are off, so round robin keeps sending every second request to the dead server.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each component has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the component is up.
Components do not know when their caller gave up; they finish the work and the answer is discarded.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: About half of the requests fail while Server B is down, because round robin keeps choosing it.
Requests that reach Server A are unaffected: their latency stays at the service time.
Failures stop the moment Server B recovers, because nothing ever took it out of rotation.
